subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Superclusters: The Largest Structures
description: A quick, practical guide to Superclusters: The Largest Structures.

hook.text: Galaxy clusters group into superclusters—the largest known structures, spanning hundreds of millions of light-years.

buildup.text: Our Milky Way belongs to the Laniakea Supercluster—a region containing 100,000 galaxies flowing toward a shared center.

discovery.text: Laniakea was mapped in 2014 by tracking galaxy motions. Its name means 'immense heaven' in Hawaiian.

twist.text: Superclusters aren't gravitationally bound. Dark energy is pulling them apart faster than gravity holds them together.

climax.text: The observable universe contains about 10 million superclusters. Beyond the horizon, there are likely many more.

punchline.text: Ten million superclusters we can see. The rest lies beyond the horizon.

quiz.question: Why are superclusters not gravitationally bound together?
options: Dark energy is pulling them apart faster than gravity can hold them
They are too far apart for gravity to have any effect
They formed from different Big Bang events

details.summary: Superclusters are enormous collections of galaxy clusters and groups spanning hundreds of millions of light-years. The Laniakea Supercluster, our cosmic address, contains over 100,000 galaxies including the Milky Way.
details.whyItMatters: Superclusters define the universe's largest gravitationally influenced structures. Mapping them reveals the cosmic web's architecture and how gravity has sculpted the distribution of matter across the observable universe.
takeaways: Superclusters span hundreds of millions of light-years
They sit at major nodes and filaments of the cosmic web

faq.question: Are superclusters gravitationally bound?
faq.answer: Mostly no. Unlike galaxy clusters, most superclusters will not remain together — dark energy's accelerating expansion will eventually pull their components apart. Only the densest inner regions may remain bound. Superclusters are transient structures in cosmic terms.

faq.question: What is the largest known structure in the universe?
faq.answer: The Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall, a vast filament of galaxy clusters spanning about 10 billion light-years. However, at such scales, 'structures' become less well-defined. The cosmic web itself is the universe's most extensive pattern, with no clear upper limit to filament networks.
